document.title: Usability Test Report - Infrared Forehead Thermometer

tests.expected_value: User installs batteries properly according to instruction for use

test_reports.conclusion: The IFT Infrared Forehead Thermometer can be used properly and easily with the user manual provided to users. No new hazards, hazardous situations, or risk scenarios are discovered, improvements are not necessary. No modification to the original design is required.

semantic_fragments.content: Score definitions for knowledge assessment: 'Correct' means participant gives a correct answer successfully aligning with success criteria; 'Incorrect' means participant gives an incorrect answer; 'Located Information' means participant is able to locate correct answer in labeling; 'Did not Locate Information' means participant is unable to locate correct answer in labeling.

Knowledge Assessment - Operation Questions: Q1: Is it easy or difficult to install the batteries? Q2: Is the user manual easy or difficult to read and understanding? Q3: Is the panel of the device easily to be recognized? Results (n=30): Q1: Very difficult 0(0%), Difficult 0(0%), Normal 2(7%), Easy 23(77%), Very easy 5(16%). Q2: Very difficult 0(0%), Difficult 0(0%), Normal 4(13%), Easy 16(53%), Very easy 10(34%). Q3: Very difficult 0(0%), Difficult 0(0%), Normal 5(17%), Easy 12(40%), Very easy 13(43%). Q4: Very difficult 0(0%), Difficult 0(0%), Normal 6(20%), Easy 13(43%), Very easy 11(37%). Q5: Very difficult 0(0%), Difficult 1(3%), Normal 8(27%), Easy 12(40%), Very easy 9(30%). Q6: Very difficult 0(0%), Difficult 0(0%), Normal 8(27%), Easy 14(47%), Very easy 8(26%).

Knowledge Assessment - Maintenance Questions: Q1: Do you think the device can be stored under -20°C? Q2: Do you think the device can be used over the temperature 40°C? Q3: Do you think the device can be used under the temperature 5°C? Q4: Do you think the device can be soaked or immersed to clean? Results (n=30): Q1: Yes 0(0%), No 30(100%), No idea 0(0%). Q2: Yes 0(0%), No 30(100%), No idea 0(0%). Q3: Yes 0(0%), No 30(100%), No idea 0(0%). Q4: Yes 0(0%), No 27(90%), No idea 3(10%).

Knowledge Assessment - Operation Environment Questions: Q1: Do you think the device can be used during examination in hospital? Q2: Do you think the device can be disturbed by cell phone or other wireless equipment? Q3: Do you think it can be used during cooking? Driving? Sleeping? Results (n=30): Q1: Yes 0(0%), No 27(90%), No idea 3(10%). Q2: Yes 3(10%), No 27(90%), No idea 0(0%). Q3: Yes 0(0%), No 26(87%), No idea 4(13%).

Knowledge Assessment - Important Indications Understanding Questions: Q1: If you have a mercury thermometer, could you use the Infrared Forehead Thermometer? Q2: If your skin broken, do you think you can still use the Infrared Forehead Thermometer? Q3: If anyone who can not express themselves or can not operate the device, do you think the device can be used by them? Results (n=30): Q1: Yes 0(0%), No 30(100%), No idea 0(0%). Q2: Yes 0(0%), No 30(100%), No idea 0(0%). Q3: Yes 0(0%), No 30(100%), No idea 0(0%).

Summative evaluation summary: 30 representative operators performed 3 tests each (90 tests total). Key findings: (1) Use error occurred within ±95% scope, device is convenient to use. (2) For maintenance, most users know how to maintain; only 3 needed to check user guide to confirm if device can be soaked or immersed to clean - risk can be avoided by checking user guide. (3) For operation environment, several users checked user manual to confirm where to use; only 3 users thought device could be disturbed by wireless equipment such as cell phone. (4) For important indications, all users could clarify conditions under which the device cannot be used.
The purpose of a summative evaluation is to assess the usability of the Infrared Forehead Thermometer device's user interface for successful task completion related to hazard-related use scenarios.
